title: Find the Punishment Number of an Integer
summary: Determine the punishment number of a positive integer n by summing the squares of all integers i from 1 to n where the square of i can be divided into substrings whose sum of integer values equals i.
statement: Determine the punishment number of a positive integer n by summing the squares of all integers i from 1 to n where the square of i can be divided into substrings whose sum of integer values equals i.
constraints: For each integer i from one through n, write the decimal digits of i squared.
i qualifies when those digits can be partitioned into contiguous nonempty pieces whose integer values sum to i.
Return the sum of i squared over all qualifying integers.
hints: For each square, recursively choose where its next decimal piece ends.
Carry the digit index and remaining sum required.
Stop successfully only when every digit is consumed and remaining equals zero; prune a piece exceeding remaining.
Every digit partition has one sequence of chosen endpoints, so exhaustive backtracking accepts exactly the qualifying squares.

tests.explanation: Qualifying values one, nine, and ten contribute 1 + 81 + 100 = 182.
Additional qualifying value 36 has square 1296 split as 1+29+6, raising the sum to 1478.
